chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (May Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: Ali ibn al-'Abbas said: al-Hasan ibn Mahbub said on the authority of Hammad ibn 'Amr al-Nasibi that: I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (AS) regarding Divine Unity, so he said:

He is the One, the Needless, the Eternal, and the Independent. He has no protection to which He may adhere, but He is the Protector of all things. He is the Knower of the unknown, known even to the ignorant. He is Unique, His creation is not in Him, nor is He in His creation. He is not sensed nor felt, and eyes cannot perceive Him. He is Elevated, yet He is Near. He is close, yet He is far. He is disobeyed, yet He forgives. He is obeyed, so He rewards. The Earth does not encompass Him, nor do His Heavens carry Him. Verily, He carries all things by means of His Omnipotence. He is perpetual, eternal, does not forget, nor wastes time, nor makes mistakes, nor plays. There is no separation for His Intent. His Judgment is His Reward, and His Command is accomplished. He does not beget to be inherited, nor is He begotten to have an associate. And there is none like unto Him.

key_terms.لَمْ يَلِدْ فِيُوْرَثْ: He does not beget to be inherited
key_terms.لَمْ يُولَدْ فَيُشَارِكَ: Nor is He begotten to have an associate

ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of Divine Unity (Tawhid) according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* serves as a cornerstone for Shia theological discourse on *Tawhid al-Siffat* (Unity of Attributes), emphasizing God's transcendence (*Tanzih*) through negation of physical form and spatial containment. It highlights the dialectical nature of Divine attributes, such as being 'high yet near,' which resolves the tension between God's absolute otherness and His immanent power, a key concept in Shia scholastic theology (*Kalam*).
